fields.features_heading: The Intake, Down to the Food Record
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds the questions, the client record behind them, and the alert that tells you an intake is in.
fields.feature_1:
A 3-day food record on the phone

Give clients three days to log meals, snacks, and drinks, with a time and a rough amount for each entry. Ask for two weekdays and one weekend day to cover both routines.
fields.feature_2:
Allergens as a checklist

Tick boxes cover the major allergens in federal food law: milk, egg, fish, crustacean shellfish, tree nuts, wheat, peanuts, soybeans, and sesame. A tick opens a reaction box.
fields.feature_3:
Supplements, one row at a time

Clients list prescriptions and supplements one row per item, with the dose and how often. Fish oil and vitamin D become two rows, not a sentence someone has to decode.
fields.feature_4:
Alerts that say an intake is ready

The app emails you or posts in Slack when a client submits, naming the client and nothing from the answers. Open the record in the app to read the food record and history.
fields.feature_5:
Signed policies at the end

Put your cancellation policy and consent to services after the last question, with a typed or drawn signature. Each signed copy is saved alongside that client's intake.
fields.feature_6:
Code you can take with you

On paid plans, export the form and its database to your GitHub repository. A developer can host it on the practice's own servers or connect it to the scheduling tool you use.

fields.usecase_heading: How Four Dietitians Put the Intake to Work
fields.tab_content_1:
Before the session, Ines has every answer

Quillan Nutrition sends the intake link with the booking email, due 2 days before the first session. Clients add goals, supplements, and food allergies, then log a 3-day food record. When Jonah Vel submits, Ines Marlow, the dietitian, gets an email that his intake is ready to review. The answers stay in the app.
fields.tab_content_2:
Of 24 rowers, 3 still owe an intake

Sunny Okafor is the dietitian for the 24 rowers at Calder College, and each one gets the same intake link before preseason. It asks for training times, usual meals, supplements, and food allergies. Her roster shows who has finished: 21 of 24 so far. The app sends the 3 who have not a reminder email with the link.
fields.tab_content_3:
After one tick, Theo's record leads with the peanut allergy

Clara Wren fills in the Little Acorn Pediatric Nutrition intake for her son Theo, with his growth goals, a 3-day food record, and the allergen checklist. She ticks peanuts and describes the reaction in the box that opens. When Hannah Brooks opens Theo's record, a banner across the top names the allergy first.
fields.tab_content_4:
By week 4, Nadia's answers sit beside her first intake

Four weeks after a first telehealth session, Bayview Table Nutrition sends each client a 5-question check-in. Nadia Osei answers on her phone about energy, skipped meals, water, the plan, and anything else. Her answers land in the same record as her first intake. Leah Ferris reads them side by side before the next call.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Nutrition Intake Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to plan a nutrition intake form around what you review before a first session, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 List what you ask at a first session
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Put the sections in reading order
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Choose a food record over a recall
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Pick who hears about a finished intake
fields.howto_step_1_des: Go through a recent first appointment and list every question you asked aloud. Mark the ones you need answered before the client arrives, and leave the rest for the session itself.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Open with contact details and goals. Health history comes next, then medications and supplements, then food allergies. Put the food record last, on its own screens, because it takes the longest to fill in.
fields.howto_step_3_des: The NCI describes a 24-hour dietary recall as a structured interview intended to capture detailed information, which suits the session itself. On the form, use a food record: a self-reported account of all foods and beverages.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Choose the dietitian or front desk person who gets the alert, and whether it comes by email or in Slack. Keep the message to the client's name and a link, and leave the food record and history in the app.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Describe the sections and who gets the alert in one plain-English prompt. Emergent builds the nutrition intake form and a database for its answers. Ask for changes the same way when a question needs rewording.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Close the form with the policies clients agree to, each beside its own signature field. Have your own counsel confirm the wording before a real client signs anything.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Test it as two made-up clients
fields.howto_step_7_des: Fill it in on a phone once with all 3 days logged and once stopping after day 1. Check that the finished intake sends the alert, the unfinished one gets a reminder, and both appear in the table.

faq_plan.q: What is a nutrition intake form?
faq_plan.a: A nutrition intake form is the questionnaire a new client completes before a first session with a dietitian or nutritionist. It asks for goals, health history, medications and supplements, and food allergies. It also records what the client eats, as a food record kept over a few ordinary days.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a nutrition intake form?
faq_plan.a: Start by listing the questions you need answered before a client's first session. Describe those sections in a plain-English prompt to Emergent's AI form builder. The form it builds opens on any phone, and changing a question later takes one more prompt.

faq_plan.q: What should a nutrition intake form template include?
faq_plan.a: A good template opens with contact details and goals. Health questions follow: past conditions, current medications and supplements, and allergies to foods. It closes with three days of logged meals and the policies a client signs. Cut any question from a template that you never read before a session.

faq_plan.q: How is a nutrition intake form different from a general client intake form?
faq_plan.a: It goes much further into health and food. A general intake, such as an accounting client intake form, sticks to who the client is and the documents to bring. A nutrition intake adds health history and a food record to read before the first session.

faq_plan.q: How far ahead of the first session should clients get a nutrition intake form?
faq_plan.a: Send it when the session is booked and make it due 2 days before. That leaves two days to go over the logged meals and follow up on anything unclear. Set a reminder email for anyone who has not submitted by the due date.

faq_plan.q: How many days of food records should a nutrition intake form ask for?
faq_plan.a: Three days is a workable length for a first intake. Longer is not always better: the NCI notes that quality of data may decline with increased number of days reported. Ask for more days later, once the client has met you.

faq_plan.q: Can a health coach use a nutrition intake form?
faq_plan.a: Yes, with fewer clinical questions. A coach can keep the goals and the food record and drop any section they will not review. For coaching that reaches past food into work and routines, a life coaching intake form fits better.

faq_plan.q: Can clients fill in a nutrition intake form on their phone?
faq_plan.a: Yes, and a phone suits the food record, since a client can log a meal right after eating it. A nutrition intake form PDF is printed or filled in a PDF reader, and its answers do not land in a database. A form Emergent builds opens in the phone's browser and keeps every entry in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: How do I keep a nutrition intake form short enough that clients finish it?
faq_plan.a: Ask only what you read before the session. Show follow-up questions only after a yes: a client with no allergies never sees the reaction box. Emergent can also build the form as a conversational flow, one question per screen.

faq_plan.q: Can a nutrition intake form ask which service a client wants?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Add a question near the top that lists what you offer, such as one-on-one counseling or a meal plan, and show only the sections that service needs. For one-off work outside client care, such as a menu review for a cafe, a project request form fits better.

Same class in faq item 8: "A nutrition intake form PDF has to be printed or filled in a PDF reader, then typed up at the practice."
findings.fix: Rewrite both as true, scoped statements, e.g. why_description: "Entries on a printed food diary stay on paper. Emergent builds a web intake that saves every answer to a database you own."; faq 8: "A nutrition intake form PDF is printed or filled in a PDF reader, and its answers do not land in a database." Search the page again for any other line about what practices or clients do.
